summary: Import-time binary dropper fetches and executes platform-specific payload from obfuscated Cloudflare Workers hosts
details: beaver-ui-actions-button 5.4.6 is advertised as a React components library, but its main module (index.js) unconditionally require()s setup.js, which on process.nextTick selects a platform-specific asset (/pkg/package, /pkg/package-arm64, /pkg/loader_mac, /pkg/package.exe), fetches it from a rotating set of Cloudflare Workers subdomains (package-proxy.cf5oob.workers.dev, package-proxy.cf8oob.workers.dev, package-proxy.cf12oob.workers.dev, package-proxy.cf17-ddb.workers.dev, package-proxy.cf25-6eb.workers.dev) with a DNS fallback under well1.site (tin/tina/ldr/win.dl.well1.site), writes the binary to /var/tmp on Unix or %TEMP% on Windows, chmods it 0755, and executes it via child_process. Hostnames and sensitive API names are constructed from split string fragments at runtime (["package-proxy.cf5oob","wor","ker.","wor","kers",".dev"].join(""), require("child_" + "process"), fs["chmod" + "Sync"]) to evade scanners. setup.js also computes an installFingerprint() SHA-256 over os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, process.cwd(), process.version, and process.pid, and forwards it as installId with the payload fetch, tagging each victim host to the RCE channel. The fetched binaries are unpinned, unsigned, from a host with no relation to the stated React-component purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
